justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a mildly bullish baseline trajectory across all three horizons. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 88.75 likely anchored closely to the most recent observed price or index level, with only modest directional drift assumed given typical short-term mean-reversion tendencies and the absence of imminent scheduled catalysts. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to 89.5, reflecting a modest positive drift assumption consistent with a modest risk premium or recent upward momentum in the underlying asset. At the one-month horizon, the estimate of 91.0 continues that gradual upward drift, essentially extrapolating a slow, steady appreciation path while acknowledging that over longer horizons, the compounding of small expected returns becomes more meaningful.

The confidence interval widths widen appropriately as the horizon extends, reflecting the fundamental statistical reality that uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly 85.5 to 92.0 is relatively tight, spanning about 6.5 units, because short-term price behavior is somewhat constrained by liquidity and market microstructure. By one week, the interval widens to about 13 units, incorporating the possibility of a macro data release, central bank communication, or geopolitical development shifting sentiment. At one month, the interval spans roughly 26 units, reflecting the full range of plausible economic scenarios, earnings outcomes, and sentiment shifts that could materialize over four weeks.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals include a surprise central bank policy action, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data such as an employment or inflation report coming in far outside consensus, or an unexpected geopolitical shock such as an escalation in an ongoing conflict or a sudden trade policy announcement. On the upside, a resolution of an existing geopolitical tension, a stronger-than-expected earnings season, or a coordinated policy stimulus could drive prices well above 104 at the one-month horizon.

It is also worth noting that my intervals assume relatively normal market functioning and liquidity. A liquidity crisis, a flash crash event, or a correlated unwind of leveraged positions could produce tail outcomes far outside even the one-month bounds I stated. Conversely, if volatility conditions were to compress dramatically due to low-volume holiday trading or a period of unusual macro calm, the realized range could end up much narrower than implied by my confidence intervals, particularly at the shorter horizons.
